We need propose a retrosynthesis route with 3 reactions for target SMILES: COc1cccc(NC(=O)c2nnn(Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3)c2N)c1

We need to construct route using available templates. We have list of templates from earlier search. The first result seems relevant: reaction_id 1014069 with retro_smarts_template that seems to break something: It appears to convert an aniline (aryl amine) attached to amide? Let's examine product_smiles from that entry: product_smiles is the target? It shows product_smiles: '[CH3:1][O:2][c:3]1[cH:4][cH:5][cH:6][c:7]([NH:8][C:9](=[O:10])[c:11]2[c:12]([NH:13][C@@H:14]([CH3:15])[c:16]3[n:17][n:18]4[cH:19][cH:20][c:21]([CH3:22])[c:23]4[c:24](=[O:25])[n:26]3-[c:27]3[cH:28][cH:29][cH:30][cH:31][cH:32]3)[n:33][cH:34][n:35][c:36]2[NH2:37])[cH:38]1'

That seems similar but with OCH3 at start (CH3O-). Our target has COc1... same OCH3. The side chain includes Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3 attached to the triazine? Actually target: COc1cccc(NC(=O)c2nnn(Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3)c2N)c1. The template product includes a methyl group attached to chiral carbon? It has [C@@H]([CH3]) etc. That seems different (maybe a different substituent). But we can still use template to disconnect amide? The retro_smarts_template: '[#7;a:8]:[c:7](-[NH2;D1;+0:9]):[c:6]-[C:4](=[O;D1;H0:5])-[#7:3]-[c;H0;D3;+0:2]1:[cH;D2;+0:1]:[c;H0;D3;+0:13](-[#8:14]-[C;D1;H3:15]):[c:12]:[c:11]:[cH;D2;+0:10]:1>>C-O-c1:[cH;D2;+0:1]:[c;H0;D3;+0:2](-[#7:3]-[C:4](=[O;D1;H0:5])-[c:6]:[c:7](:[#7;a:8])-[NH;D2;+0:9]-C-[c;H0;D3;+0:10]2:[c:11]:[c:12]:[c;H0;D3;+0:13](-[#8:14]-[C;D1;H3:15]):c:c:2):c:c:c:1'

Seems to be a reverse of a Friedel-Crafts acylation? Hard to parse.

We need 3 steps: maybe (1) disconnection of amide to give aniline and acyl chloride (or acid). (2) disconnection of the aryl-alkyl bond linking the phenyl to the triazine via a SN2? Actually the side chain is Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3 attached to the triazine nitrogen? The triazine has a substituent Cc3... which is a benzyl attached to phenyl with a side chain containing a tertiary amine (azetidine? Actually N4CC(F)C4 is a azetidine with fluorine). That could be formed via SN2 of benzyl chloride with amine.

So propose retrosynthesis:

Step1: Break amide: target -> aniline (COc1cccc(NH2)c1) + acyl fragment (c2nnn(Cc3... )c2N)C(=O)Cl? Actually amide formed from aniline and acyl chloride of heterocycle. So retro step: amide disconnection (Friedel-Crafts acylation? Actually amide formation is condensation of amine with acid chloride). So template likely for amide formation (functional groups broken: amine, acyl chloride; formed: amide). Use template ID maybe 1014069? That seems to involve amide formation from aniline and acyl chloride? Let's check: The retro_smarts_template shows [#7;a:8]:[c:7](-[NH2...])... So it takes an aniline with NH2 and attaches to carbonyl etc. So yes.

Thus step1: target -> precursor A (aniline with OMe) and precursor B (acyl chloride of heterocycle). Precursor A SMILES: COc1cccc(NH2)c1 (anisidine). Precursor B SMILES: ClC(=O)c2nnn(Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3)c2N (acyl chloride). Need to verify if template works.

Step2: Disconnection of the benzyl linkage: precursor B contains Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3 attached to triazine nitrogen via a carbon (benzyl). Could be formed by SN2 of benzyl chloride with amine (the N of the azetidine?). Actually the side chain is Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3 attached to triazine N as substituent: N-CH2-aryl. So we can disconnect at the C-N bond: benzyl chloride + amine (N4CC(F)C4). So precursor B' -> heterocycle with N-H (instead of N-CH2-aryl) and benzyl chloride (ClCH2-aryl). The heterocycle precursor: c2nnn(Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3)c2N becomes c2nnn(Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3)c2N? Wait the N attached to benzyl is part of heterocycle? Actually the heterocycle is a 1,2,4-triazine? The substituent is Cc3... attached to N of triazine? The SMILES: c2nnn(Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3)c2N. So the triazine has an N attached to a benzyl group (C- attached to aromatic). So SN2 could form that C-N bond by reacting benzyl chloride with the triazine N-H (or maybe the N is part of heterocycle). So precursor after step2: heterocycle with NH (instead of N-CH2-aryl) i.e., c2nnn(C)?? Actually the substituent is Cc3... So after disconnection, we have heterocycle with N-H (or N-? ) and benzyl chloride (ClCH2-aryl). So we need to generate benzyl chloride precursor: ClCH2c3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3.

Step3: The azetidine fragment (N4CC(F)C4) attached to phenyl via CH2NH. That could be formed via SN2 of the phenyl amine (aniline) with azetidine? Actually we have phenyl-CH2-N(azetidine). The precursor could be phenyl-CH2-Cl (benzyl chloride) reacting with azetidine amine (N4CC(F)C4). But we already used benzyl chloride in step2. Actually the benzyl chloride is attached to phenyl which also has side chain CN4... So the benzyl chloride already includes the azetidine attached? Wait the benzyl chloride we propose is ClCH2-aryl where aryl has substituent CN4... So the azetidine is attached via a CH2 to the phenyl (C N4...). That is part of the benzyl chloride? The SMILES: Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3. This is a phenyl with a side chain CH2-N(azetidine). The benzyl carbon attached to triazine is the first C of that group (the C attached to triazine). So the benzyl carbon is attached to phenyl ring (the same phenyl). So the benzyl chloride would be ClCH2-aryl where the aryl already has the side chain CN4... So step2 could be SN2 between that benzyl chloride and the triazine N-H.

Thus step3 could be formation of the side chain CN4CC(F)C4 via SN2 of the phenyl CH2 (attached to phenyl) with azetidine? Actually the side chain is CH2-N(azetidine). Could be formed by SN2 of phenyl bromomethyl (or chloride) with azetidine amine. So we need a precursor phenyl-CH2-Br (or Cl) and azetidine (N4CC(F)C4). So step3: phenyl-CH2-Br + azetidine -> phenyl-CH2-N(azetidine). That matches SN2.

Thus overall 3 steps: (1) amide formation (condensation) between anisidine and heterocycle acyl chloride. (2) SN2 between triazine N-H and benzyl chloride (aryl with side chain). (3) SN2 between phenyl-CH2-X and azetidine.

We need template IDs for SN2 and amide formation. We have template ID 1014069 for amide formation (maybe). For SN2, we need a template that breaks alkyl halide and forms C-N. Search for functional_groups_broken ["alkyl halide"], functional_groups_formed ["secondary amines"] maybe. Let's search.
